nodes.name: Subdivision (topological minor)
nodes.statement: A \emph{subdivision} or \emph{topological minor} of a graph $F$, denoted by $TF$, is a graph obtained by replacing the edges of $F$ with internally vertex-disjoint paths between endpoints.
differentia: obtained by replacing the edges of $F$ with internally vertex-disjoint paths between endpoints

nodes.name: Mader's theorem on topological cliques
nodes.statement: A classical result of Mader~\cite{mader} from 1972 states that there is some function $f(d)$ of $d$ such that any graph with average degree $f(d)$ contains a copy of $TK_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Some function $f(d)$ of average degree forces a subdivision of $K_d$.

nodes.name: Mader / Erdős–Hajnal conjecture on topological cliques
nodes.statement: Mader, and independently Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal~\cite{eh}, conjectured that the correct order of magnitude for $f(d)$ is $d^2$.
conclusions: the correct order of magnitude for $f(d)$ is $d^2$

nodes.name: Kühn–Osthus topological clique theorem
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree at least $(1+o(1))\frac{10}{23} d^2$. Then $G \supseteq TK_d$.
assumptions: $G$ be a graph with average degree at least $(1+o(1))\frac{10}{23} d^2$
nodes.label: btks

nodes.name: Jung's tightness example
nodes.statement: This result is tight up to the constant factor; as Jung~\cite{jung} observed, the complete bipartite graph $K_{r,r}$ with $r = \lfloor d^2/8 \rfloor$ does not contain a copy of $TK_{d+1}$.
conclusions: the complete bipartite graph $K_{r,r}$ with $r = \lfloor d^2/8 \rfloor$ does not contain a copy of $TK_{d+1}$

nodes.name: Distinguishable subgraphs
nodes.statement: We say that two subgraphs $H,H'$ of a graph $G$ are \emph{distinguishable} if $V(H) \neq V(H')$.

nodes.name: Komlós's conjecture on distinguishable cycles
nodes.statement: In 1981, Koml\'os~(see~\cite{tuza2}) conjectured that every graph with minimum degree $d$ contains at least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{d+1}$,\footnote{Koml\'os's conjecture has recently been resolved by J.~Kim and the authors, see~\cite{KLShS}.} that is, $2^{d+1}-{d+1\choose 2}-d-2$.
conclusions: contains at least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{d+1}$

nodes.name: Tuza's exponential distinguishable cycles bound
nodes.statement: A weaker conjecture, asking whether minimum degree $d$ forces exponential in $d$ many distinguishable cycles, was verified by Tuza~\cite{tuza2} who obtained a lower bound $2^{\lfloor(d+4)/2\rfloor}-O(d^2)$ for graphs with average degree $d$.

nodes.name: Tuza's distinguishable cycles theorem for triangle-dense graphs
nodes.statement: If instead one imposes a different local condition on $G$: that every edge lies in at least $t$ triangles; it is shown in~\cite{tuza2} that $G$ contains as least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{t+2}$.
assumptions: every edge lies in at least $t$ triangles
conclusions: $G$ contains as least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{t+2}$

nodes.name: $(F,t)$-locally dense graph
nodes.statement: To formulate this more precisely, let us say that a graph $G$ is \emph{$(F,t)$-locally dense} if every edge $e$ of $G$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $F$.
differentia: every edge $e$ of $G$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $F$

nodes.name: $s(F,G)$: largest distinguishable family of subdivisions
nodes.statement: Write $s(F,G)$ for the size of the largest collection of distinguishable subdivisions of $F$ in $G$.

nodes.name: $s_t(F)$
nodes.statement:
Define 
$$s_t(F)=\min\{ s(F,G) : G  \mbox{ is } (F,t)\mbox{-locally dense}\}.$$
also_stated_at: Given a graph $F$, let $s_t(F)$ be the number of subdivisions of $F$, each with a different vertex set, which one can guarantee in a graph $G$ in which every edge lies in at least $t$ copies of $F$.
nodes.statement_short: $s_t(F)$ is the minimum of $s(F,G)$ over all $(F,t)$-locally dense graphs $G$.

nodes.name: Tuza's question on exponentially many subdivisions
nodes.statement: Tuza's question~\cite{tuza2} was for which graphs $F$ one can find $c,c' > 0$ such that whenever $t$ is a sufficiently large integer compared to $|F|$, we have $s_t(F) \geq c^{t^{c'}}$.
nodes.statement_short: For which $F$ is $s_t(F)$ at least exponential in a power of $t$?

nodes.name: Local conditions for exponentially many subdivisions (main theorem)
nodes.statement: Let $\ell \geq 3$ be an integer. Whenever $t$ is sufficiently large, the following hold. \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $s_t(K_\ell) \geq 2^{t^{c'}}$, where $c':=c'(\ell) \geq \frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}$. \item[(ii)] For all graphs $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which are not complete, $$s_t(F) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}.$$ \item[(iii)] Whenever $\ell \geq 4$, we have $$s_t(K_\ell^-) \geq t^{(1-o(1))(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)},$$ where $K_\ell^-$ is the graph obtained from $K_\ell$ by removing an edge.\footnote{Here $o(1)$ denotes a function which tends to $0$ as $t \to \infty$.} \end{itemize}
assumptions: For all graphs $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which are not complete
For all graphs $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which are not complete

nodes.statement_short: Cliques $K_\ell$ force exponentially many distinguishable subdivisions under the local condition; every non-complete $F$ admits only polynomially many; $K_\ell^-$ needs a polynomial of nearly matching degree.
nodes.label: main

nodes.name: Optimality of $c'(\ell)$ up to a factor 1/2
nodes.statement: For part (i), our bound on $c'(\ell)$ is best possible up to the constant factor $\frac{1}{2}$.
conclusions: our bound on $c'(\ell)$ is best possible up to the constant factor $\frac{1}{2}$

nodes.name: Tuza's upper bound on $c'(\ell)$
nodes.statement: As noted by Tuza~\cite{tuza}, $c'(\ell) \leq \frac{1}{\ell-2}$.

nodes.name: Complete graph $K_r$ attains Tuza's bound
nodes.statement:
This is attained by the graph $G = K_r$, where $r$ satisfies $\binom{r-2}{\ell-2} = t$.
Indeed, every edge of $G$ lies in exactly $t$ copies of $K_\ell$, and every set $X \subseteq V(G)$ of size at least $\ell$ is such that there is a copy of $TK_\ell$ with vertex set $X$.
Therefore,
$$
s_t(K_{\ell},G) = \sum_{i=\ell}^{r} \binom{r}{i} \leq 2^r \leq 2^{t^{\frac{1}{\ell-2}}}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Take $G=K_r$ with $\binom{r-2}{\ell-2}=t$; every vertex set of size at least $\ell$ carries a $TK_\ell$, giving at most $2^r$ subdivisions.

nodes.name: Polynomial upper bound is near-optimal
nodes.statement:
Part (ii) shows that for all non-complete $F$, the minimum number of distinguishable subdivisions of $F$ among all $(F,t)$-locally dense graphs is at most a polynomial in $t$.
Our upper bound on $s_t(F)$ in (ii) is close to being optimal, as shown by part (iii).

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 2
nodes.statement:
Let us briefly sketch the ideas in the proof.
For part (i), first note that a $(K_\ell,t)$-locally dense graph $G$ has minimum degree which is polynomial in $t$.
Then Theorem~\ref{btks} furnishes us with a subdivision $T$ of $K_d$ in $G$ such that $d$ is polynomial in $t$.
Every subset of the branch vertices of $T$ which has order at least $\ell$ gives rise to a subdivision of $K_\ell$, and all of these are distinguishable.
For part (ii), for each non-complete $F$ we construct a graph $G$ which is $(F,t)$-locally dense but has a very small dominating set $A$ (so each copy of $F$ has very large overlap).
The size of $A$ limits the number of vertices in any subdivision which lie outside of $A$.
The proof of (iii) combines ideas from the previous parts together with an averaging argument.
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: (i) min degree polynomial in $t$ plus Kühn–Osthus gives a large clique subdivision; (ii) a construction with a tiny dominating set; (iii) averaging.

nodes.name: Branch vertices
nodes.statement: We call those vertices of $TF$ which correspond to those of $F$ the \emph{branch vertices}.\footnote{We use standard graph theoretic notation. For natural numbers $k \leq \ell$, write $[\ell] := \lbrace 1,\ldots, \ell \rbrace$ and write $\binom{[\ell]}{k}$ for the set of $k$-subsets of $[\ell]$.}

nodes.name: Clique subdivisions contain smaller ones through all branch vertices
nodes.statement: Let $k,\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ with $\ell \leq k$ and suppose that $T$ is a subdivision of $K_k$. Then $T$ contains a subdivision of $K_\ell$ which contains all branch vertices of $T$.
conclusions: $T$ contains a subdivision of $K_\ell$ which contains all branch vertices of $T$
nodes.label: easy

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ be the branch vertices of $K_k$ in $T$. Now $T$ is the union of a set $\lbrace P(i,j): ij \in \binom{[k]}{2} \rbrace$ of internally vertex-disjoint paths where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i, x_j$. Then we can find a copy of $TK_\ell$ with branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ by taking the paths $P(i,j)$ for all $\lbrace i,j \rbrace \in \binom{[\ell]}{2} \setminus \lbrace 1,\ell \rbrace$, and taking the concatenation of the paths $P(\ell,\ell+1), P(\ell+1,\ell+2), \ldots, P(k-1,k),P(1,k)$ to obtain a path between $x_1$ and $x_\ell$ which contains every other branch vertex in $V(T)$. \hfill$\blacksquare$
nodes.statement_short: Keep paths among the first $\ell$ branch vertices and replace the $x_1x_\ell$ path by a concatenation through all other branch vertices.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement:
Fix $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$.
We will first prove (i).
We may assume that $\ell \geq 4$ since the statement is known for $\ell = 3$ (see \cite{tuza2}).
Let $G$ be $(K_\ell,t)$-locally dense, that is, every edge $xy \in E(G)$ lies in at least $t$ copies if $K_\ell$.
Then
\begin{equation} t \le \binom{|N(x) \cap N(y)|}{\ell-2}\le \binom{d(x)}{\ell-2} < \left( \frac{d(x) \cdot e}{\ell-2} \right)^{\ell-2}
\end{equation}
and so $d(x) > e^{-1}(\ell-2)t^{\frac{1}{\ell-2}}$ for all $x \in V(G)$ which are not isolated. Now Theorem~\ref{btks} implies that $G$ contains a copy of $TK_d$, where
\begin{equation} d = (1-o(1))\sqrt{\frac{23(\ell-2)}{10e}}\cdot t^{\frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}.
\end{equation}
Let $X := \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_d \rbrace$ be the set of branch vertices of this copy of $TK_d$ and let $P(i,j)$, $ij \in \binom{[d]}{2}$, be the internally vertex-disjoint path between $x_i$ and $x_j$.


Do the following for each $I \subseteq [d]$ with $|I| \geq \ell$.
Let $X_I := \lbrace x_i : i \in I \rbrace$.
Let $T_I$ be the subdivision of $K_{|I|}$ whose set of branch vertices is precisely $X_I$ and which consists of paths $P(i,j)$ with $ij \in \binom{I}{2}$.
So $V(T_I) \cap X = X_I$.
Proposition~\ref{easy} implies that $T_I$ contains a subgraph $S_I$ which is a subdivision of $K_\ell$ such that $V(S_I) \cap X = X_I$.
Thus obtain a collection $\lbrace S_I : I \subseteq [d], |I| \geq \ell \rbrace$ of subdivisions of $K_\ell$ in $G$.
This collection is distinguishable because $V(S_I) \cap X \neq V(S_{I'}) \cap X$ for distinct $I,I' \subseteq [d]$.
So, when $t$ is sufficiently large,
$$
s(F,G) \geq 2^d - \sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1} \binom{d}{i} \geq 2^d - (d+1)^{\ell-1} \geq 2^{t^{\frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}},
$$
where we used the fact that $\ell \geq 4$ in~(\ref{d}).
This
completes the proof of part (i) of Theorem~\ref{main}.



\medskip
\noindent
We now turn to the proof of (ii), which will follow from the next lemma.

\begin{lemma} Let $G$ be a graph with vertex partition $A \cup B$, where $B$ is an independent set.
Let $F$ be a graph on $\ell \geq |A|$ vertices.
Then $s(F,G) \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}$.
\end{lemma}

\medskip
\noindent
\emph{Proof.}
Write $V(F) = [\ell]$.
Let $T$ be a subdivision of $F$ in $G$, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ be its branch vertices.
So $T$ consists of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(F)$, where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i,x_j$.
Denote by $\mathcal{P}$ the union of the $P(i,j)$.
Let $\mathcal{P}(A,A)$ be the set of $P(i,j)$ such that $x_i,x_j \in A$, and define $\mathcal{P}(A,B) = \mathcal{P}(B,A)$ and $\mathcal{P}(B,B)$ analogously.
Given $P = P(i,j)$, let $a_P$ be the number of internal vertices of $P$ which lie in $A$, i.e.~$a_P := |A \cap (V(P)\setminus \lbrace x_i,x_j \rbrace)|$ and define $b_P$ analogously for $B$.
Since $B$ is an independent set, the following relationships are easy to see:
\begin{align*}
b_P &\leq a_P+1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,A);\\
b_P &\leq a_P \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,B);\\
b_P &\leq a_P-1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(B,B).
\end{align*}
Then, since $|\mathcal{P}|= e(F)$,
\begin{align*}
\ell \geq |A| \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}a_P \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}(b_P-1)=\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P-|\mathcal{P}|\quad \Rightarrow \quad \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \le \ell+|\mathcal{P}|= \ell+e(F).
\end{align*}
Denote by $b^*$ the number of branch vertices of $T$ which lie in $B$. Clearly, $b^*\le \ell$, hence, 
$$|V(T) \cap B| = b^* + \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \leq 2\ell + e(F).$$

Therefore an upper bound for $s(F,G)$ can be obtained by counting the number of subsets of $V(G)$ containing at most $2\ell+e(F)$ vertices in $B$.
Thus
$$
s(F,G) \leq 2^{|A|} \cdot \sum_{i = 0}^{2\ell + e(F)} \binom{|B|}{i} \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell},
$$
proving the lemma.
\hfill$\blacksquare$

\medskip
\noindent
We will construct a graph $G$ for which $s(F,G) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$, via Lemma~\ref{semibip}.
Let $A,B$ be disjoint sets of vertices with $|A|=\ell-2$ and $|B| = t+1$, and let $V(G) = A \cup B$.
Add every edge to $G$ with at least one endpoint in $A$.
For any graph $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which is not complete, we claim that $G$ is $(F,t)$-locally dense.
It suffices to show that $G$ is $(K_\ell^- ,t)$-locally dense. Let $e$ be the non-adjacent pair in $K_\ell^-$ and let $xy \in E(G)$.
If $x,y \in A$, then for any of the $\binom{t+1}{2}>t$ pairs $\lbrace w,z \rbrace$ of vertices in $B$, we have that $G[A \cup \lbrace w,z \rbrace]$ is isomorphic to $K_\ell^-$ with $wz$ playing the role of $e$.
Without loss of generality, the only other case is $x \in A$, $y \in B$.
Then similarly we can choose any of the $t$ vertices $w \in B \setminus \lbrace y \rbrace$ so that $wy$ plays the role of the missing edge $e$.
Therefore every edge $xy \in E(G)$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $K_\ell^-$, and hence $F$.
Now Lemma~\ref{semibip} implies that $s_t(F) \leq s(F,G) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$, as required.

\medskip
\noindent
Finally, we prove (iii).
Let ${\varepsilon} > 0$ and let $t$ be sufficiently large compared to ${\varepsilon}$.
Let $G$ be $(K_\ell^-,t)$-locally dense.
We will show that $s(K_\ell^-,G) \geq t^{(1-2{\varepsilon})(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)}$.
For each edge $e \in E(G)$, let $g(e)$ be the number of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ in $G$ which contain $e$.
Suppose first that $g(e) \geq t^{{\varepsilon}}$ for all $e \in E(G)$.
Then $G$ is $(K_{\ell-1},t^{{\varepsilon}})$-locally dense.
So, by (\ref{d}) and Theorem~\ref{btks}, $G$ contains a copy of $K_d$, where $d = (\sqrt{\ell}/3) t^{{\varepsilon}/(2(\ell-3))}$.
The same argument as (i) shows that
$$
s(K_\ell^-,G) \geq s(K_\ell,G) \geq 2^d - (d+1)^{\ell-1} \geq 2^{\frac{1}{2}t^{\frac{{\varepsilon}}{2(\ell-3)}}} > t^{\ell^2}
$$
whenever $t$ is sufficiently large compared to ${\varepsilon}$ and $\ell$ (and recall that $\ell \geq 4$).

So we may assume that there is some $e \in E(G)$ with $g(e) < t^{{\varepsilon}}$.

\begin{claim}
There is a subgraph $H$ of $G$ with vertex partition $A \cup B$ where $|A|=\ell-1$ and $|B| \geq 2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}/(\ell-1)$, such that $H[A]$ is complete and there is $z \in A$ such that $H[A\setminus \lbrace z \rbrace, B]$ is a complete bipartite graph.
\end{claim}

\medskip
\noindent
\emph{Proof.}
Let $\mathcal{J}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ containing $e$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell}^-$ containing $e$.
So $|\mathcal{J}| = g(e)$ and $|\mathcal{K}| \geq t$.
Now, every copy of $K_\ell^-$ containing $e$ contains exactly two distinct $J \in \mathcal{J}$ as subgraphs.
So, by averaging, there is some $J \in \mathcal{J}$ such that there is $\mathcal{K}' \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ with the property that $J \subseteq K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ and
\begin{equation} |\mathcal{K}'| \geq \frac{2|\mathcal{K}|}{g(e)}\ge 2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}.
\end{equation}
Every $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ has exactly one non-adjacent pair, and exactly one member of this pair lies in $V(J)$.
Averaging once again we see that there is some $z \in V(J)$ and $\mathcal{K}'' \subseteq \mathcal{K}'$ such that for all $K \in \mathcal{K}''$ every $y \in V(K)$ is incident with every $x \in V(J) \setminus \lbrace z \rbrace$; and
$$
|\mathcal{K}''| \geq \frac{|\mathcal{K}'|}{\ell-1} \stackrel{(\ref{K})}{\geq} \frac{2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}}{\ell-1}.
$$
Now, let $A := V(J)$ and let $B := \bigcup_{K \in \mathcal{K}''}V(K) \setminus V(J)$.
Every $K \in \mathcal{K''}$ contains precisely one vertex $x_K$ outside of $V(J)$ and the only non-adjacent pair in $K$ is $x_Kz$.
Therefore the vertices $x_K$ are distinct for distinct $K$.
So $|B| = |\mathcal{K}''|$, as required.
The remaining properties are clear.
\hfill$\blacksquare$

\medskip
\noindent
It will suffice to give a lower bound for $s(K_\ell^-,H)$.
We will count the number of subdivisions $T$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with specific properties.
Label the vertices of $K_\ell^-$ by $1,\ldots,\ell$, where $E(K_\ell^-) = \binom{[\ell]}{2}\setminus \lbrace \ell-1,\ell \rbrace$.
Write $A = \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_{\ell-1} := z \rbrace$.
Let $x_\ell$ and $x_{ij}$ for all $ij \in \binom{[\ell-2]}{2}$ be arbitrary distinct vertices in $B$ and let $X$ be the set consisting of these vertices.
Using these we can find a subdivision $T(X)$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with vertex set $A \cup X$, branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ and paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(K_\ell^-)$, as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item For all $i \in [\ell-1]$, the vertex $x_i \in A$ corresponds to $i \in V(K_\ell^-)$, and the vertex $x_\ell \in B$ corresponds to $\ell \in V(K_\ell^-)$.
\item For all $ij \in \binom{[\ell-2]}{2}$, each $P(i,j)$ has precisely one internal vertex $x_{ij}$, which lies in $B$. For all $i \in [\ell-2]$ and $j \in \lbrace \ell-1,\ell \rbrace$, $P(i,j)$ is the edge $x_ix_j$. 
\end{itemize}
Note that $T(X)$ exists because $H[A]$ is complete and $H[A \setminus \lbrace x_{\ell-1} \rbrace,B]$ is complete bipartite. Different choices of $X$ give rise to distinguishable $T(X)$ since $V(T(X)) = A \cup X$.
Each $X$ has order $\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1$, so
\begin{eqnarray*}
s(K_\ell^-,G) &\geq& s(K_\ell^-,H) \geq \binom{|B|}{\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1} \geq \left(\frac{2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}}{(\ell-1)\left(\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1\right)}\right)^{\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1}\\
& \geq &t^{(1-2{\varepsilon})\left(\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1\right)}= t^{(1-2{\varepsilon})(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)},
\end{eqnarray*}
completing the proof of (iii).
This concludes the proof of Theorem~\ref{main}.
\hfill$\square$
nodes.statement_short: (i) Degree bound plus Kühn–Osthus gives $TK_d$, whose branch-vertex subsets give distinguishable $TK_\ell$; (ii) semi-bipartite construction plus Lemma 4; (iii) dichotomy on $K_{\ell-1}$ counts. Key step in (iii): averaging gives the structured subgraph $H$ of Claim 5.

Given $P = P(i,j)$, let $a_P$ be the number of internal vertices of $P$ which lie in $A$, i.e.~$a_P := |A \cap (V(P)\setminus \lbrace x_i,x_j \rbrace)|$ and define $b_P$ analogously for $B$. Since $B$ is an independent set, the following relationships are easy to see: \begin{align*} b_P &\leq a_P+1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,A);\\ b_P &\leq a_P \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,B);\\ b_P &\leq a_P-1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(B,B). \end{align*} Then, since $|\mathcal{P}|= e(F)$, \begin{align*} \ell \geq |A| \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}a_P \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}(b_P-1)=\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P-|\mathcal{P}|\quad \Rightarrow \quad \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \le \ell+|\mathcal{P}|= \ell+e(F). \end{align*} Denote by $b^*$ the number of branch vertices of $T$ which lie in $B$. Clearly, $b^*\le \ell$, hence, $$|V(T) \cap B| = b^* + \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \leq 2\ell + e(F).$$ Therefore an upper bound for $s(F,G)$ can be obtained by counting the number of subsets of $V(G)$ containing at most $2\ell+e(F)$ vertices in $B$. Thus $$ s(F,G) \leq 2^{|A|} \cdot \sum_{i = 0}^{2\ell + e(F)} \binom{|B|}{i} \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}, $$ proving the lemma. \hfill$\blacksquare$

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{J}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ containing $e$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell}^-$ containing $e$.
So $|\mathcal{J}| = g(e)$ and $|\mathcal{K}| \geq t$.
Now, every copy of $K_\ell^-$ containing $e$ contains exactly two distinct $J \in \mathcal{J}$ as subgraphs.
So, by averaging, there is some $J \in \mathcal{J}$ such that there is $\mathcal{K}' \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ with the property that $J \subseteq K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ and
\begin{equation} |\mathcal{K}'| \geq \frac{2|\mathcal{K}|}{g(e)}\ge 2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}.
\end{equation}
Every $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ has exactly one non-adjacent pair, and exactly one member of this pair lies in $V(J)$.
Averaging once again we see that there is some $z \in V(J)$ and $\mathcal{K}'' \subseteq \mathcal{K}'$ such that for all $K \in \mathcal{K}''$ every $y \in V(K)$ is incident with every $x \in V(J) \setminus \lbrace z \rbrace$; and
$$
|\mathcal{K}''| \geq \frac{|\mathcal{K}'|}{\ell-1} \stackrel{(\ref{K})}{\geq} \frac{2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}}{\ell-1}.
$$
Now, let $A := V(J)$ and let $B := \bigcup_{K \in \mathcal{K}''}V(K) \setminus V(J)$.
Every $K \in \mathcal{K''}$ contains precisely one vertex $x_K$ outside of $V(J)$ and the only non-adjacent pair in $K$ is $x_Kz$.
Therefore the vertices $x_K$ are distinct for distinct $K$.
So $|B| = |\mathcal{K}''|$, as required.
The remaining properties are clear.

nodes.name: $(F,k,t)$-locally dense graph
nodes.statement:
Given a graph $F$ on $\ell$ vertices, for each $3 \leq k \leq \ell$, we make the following definition. 
We say that a graph $G$ is \emph{$(F,k,t)$-locally dense} if every edge of $G$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $F'$ for all subgraphs $F' \subseteq F$ with $|F'| \geq k$.

nodes.name: $(F,\ell,t)$-local density equals $(F,t)$-local density

nodes.name: Characterisation for $(F,k,t)$-locally dense hosts
nodes.statement: Let $\ell,k \in \mathbb{N}$ and $3 \leq k \leq \ell$. Then, whenever $t$ is sufficiently large, the following hold. \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] For all graphs $F$ containing a copy of $K_k$, we have that $s_t(F,k) \geq 2^{t^{c'(k)}}$, where $c'(k) \geq \frac{1}{2(k-2)}$. \item[(ii)] For all $K_k$-free graphs $F$, we have that $s_t(F,k) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$. \end{itemize}

For all graphs $F$ containing a copy of $K_k$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6

nodes.statement:
Therefore it would be of interest to restate the question of Tuza with an entirely different local condition.

nodes.statement:

Let $\mathcal{J}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ containing $e$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell}^-$ containing $e$.

Averaging once again we see that there is some $z \in V(J)$ and $\mathcal{K}'' \subseteq \mathcal{K}'$ such that for all $K \in \mathcal{K}''$ every $y \in V(K)$ is incident with every $x \in V(J) \setminus \lbrace z \rbrace$; and

|\mathcal{K}''| \geq \frac{|\mathcal{K}'|}{\ell-1} \stackrel{(\ref{K})}{\geq} \frac{2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}}{\ell-1}.
$$

Now, let $A := V(J)$ and let $B := \bigcup_{K \in \mathcal{K}''}V(K) \setminus V(J)$.

nodes.name: Part (i)
nodes.statement:
For (i), let $F$ be a graph on $\ell$ vertices containing a copy of $K_k$.
Let $G$ be a $(F,k,t)$-locally dense graph.
Then $G$ is certainly $(K_k,t)$-locally dense.
The conclusion follows immediately from Theorem~\ref{main}(i).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $(K_k,t)$-local density and apply Theorem 2(i).

nodes.name: Part (ii)
nodes.statement:
For (ii), note that $F$ is $K_k$-free if and only if every subgraph $F' \subseteq F$ with $|F'| \geq k$ is such that $F'$ contains a pair of non-adjacent vertices.
Therefore the graph $G$ we constructed in the proof of Theorem~\ref{main}(ii) is in fact $(F,k,t)$-dense.
(To see this, one can use the same argument, as there is always a non-adjacent pair in $F'$ which can we embed into $B$ in at least $t$ different ways.) The conclusion follows from Lemma~\ref{semibip}.

nodes.name: Proof of part (i)
nodes.statement:
Fix $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$.
We will first prove (i).
We may assume that $\ell \geq 4$ since the statement is known for $\ell = 3$ (see \cite{tuza2}).
Let $G$ be $(K_\ell,t)$-locally dense, that is, every edge $xy \in E(G)$ lies in at least $t$ copies if $K_\ell$.
Then
\begin{equation} t \le \binom{|N(x) \cap N(y)|}{\ell-2}\le \binom{d(x)}{\ell-2} < \left( \frac{d(x) \cdot e}{\ell-2} \right)^{\ell-2}
\end{equation}
and so $d(x) > e^{-1}(\ell-2)t^{\frac{1}{\ell-2}}$ for all $x \in V(G)$ which are not isolated. Now Theorem~\ref{btks} implies that $G$ contains a copy of $TK_d$, where
\begin{equation} d = (1-o(1))\sqrt{\frac{23(\ell-2)}{10e}}\cdot t^{\frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}.
\end{equation}
Let $X := \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_d \rbrace$ be the set of branch vertices of this copy of $TK_d$ and let $P(i,j)$, $ij \in \binom{[d]}{2}$, be the internally vertex-disjoint path between $x_i$ and $x_j$.


Do the following for each $I \subseteq [d]$ with $|I| \geq \ell$.
Let $X_I := \lbrace x_i : i \in I \rbrace$.
Let $T_I$ be the subdivision of $K_{|I|}$ whose set of branch vertices is precisely $X_I$ and which consists of paths $P(i,j)$ with $ij \in \binom{I}{2}$.
So $V(T_I) \cap X = X_I$.
Proposition~\ref{easy} implies that $T_I$ contains a subgraph $S_I$ which is a subdivision of $K_\ell$ such that $V(S_I) \cap X = X_I$.
Thus obtain a collection $\lbrace S_I : I \subseteq [d], |I| \geq \ell \rbrace$ of subdivisions of $K_\ell$ in $G$.
This collection is distinguishable because $V(S_I) \cap X \neq V(S_{I'}) \cap X$ for distinct $I,I' \subseteq [d]$.
So, when $t$ is sufficiently large,
$$
s(F,G) \geq 2^d - \sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1} \binom{d}{i} \geq 2^d - (d+1)^{\ell-1} \geq 2^{t^{\frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}},
$$
where we used the fact that $\ell \geq 4$ in~(\ref{d}).
This
completes the proof of part (i) of Theorem~\ref{main}.
nodes.statement_short: Prove part (i) via a large clique subdivision.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\ell\ge4$
nodes.statement:
Fix $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$.
We will first prove (i).
We may assume that $\ell \geq 4$ since the statement is known for $\ell = 3$ (see \cite{tuza2}).

nodes.name: Minimum degree bound

nodes.name: Apply Kühn–Osthus
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1 yields a $TK_d$ with $d$ polynomial in $t$.

Let $X := \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_d \rbrace$ be the set of branch vertices of this copy of $TK_d$ and let $P(i,j)$, $ij \in \binom{[d]}{2}$, be the internally vertex-disjoint path between $x_i$ and $x_j$.

So $V(T_I) \cap X = X_I$.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 3
nodes.statement:
Proposition~\ref{easy} implies that $T_I$ contains a subgraph $S_I$ which is a subdivision of $K_\ell$ such that $V(S_I) \cap X = X_I$.

nodes.name: Count
nodes.statement:
So, when $t$ is sufficiently large,
$$
s(F,G) \geq 2^d - \sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1} \binom{d}{i} \geq 2^d - (d+1)^{\ell-1} \geq 2^{t^{\frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}},

where we used the fact that $\ell \geq 4$ in~(\ref{d}).

nodes.name: Proof of part (ii)
nodes.statement:
We now turn to the proof of (ii), which will follow from the next lemma.

\begin{lemma} Let $G$ be a graph with vertex partition $A \cup B$, where $B$ is an independent set.
Let $F$ be a graph on $\ell \geq |A|$ vertices.
Then $s(F,G) \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}$.
\end{lemma}

\medskip
\noindent
\emph{Proof.}
Write $V(F) = [\ell]$.
Let $T$ be a subdivision of $F$ in $G$, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ be its branch vertices.
So $T$ consists of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(F)$, where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i,x_j$.
Denote by $\mathcal{P}$ the union of the $P(i,j)$.
Let $\mathcal{P}(A,A)$ be the set of $P(i,j)$ such that $x_i,x_j \in A$, and define $\mathcal{P}(A,B) = \mathcal{P}(B,A)$ and $\mathcal{P}(B,B)$ analogously.
Given $P = P(i,j)$, let $a_P$ be the number of internal vertices of $P$ which lie in $A$, i.e.~$a_P := |A \cap (V(P)\setminus \lbrace x_i,x_j \rbrace)|$ and define $b_P$ analogously for $B$.
Since $B$ is an independent set, the following relationships are easy to see:
\begin{align*}
b_P &\leq a_P+1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,A);\\
b_P &\leq a_P \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,B);\\
b_P &\leq a_P-1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(B,B).
\end{align*}
Then, since $|\mathcal{P}|= e(F)$,
\begin{align*}
\ell \geq |A| \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}a_P \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}(b_P-1)=\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P-|\mathcal{P}|\quad \Rightarrow \quad \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \le \ell+|\mathcal{P}|= \ell+e(F).
\end{align*}
Denote by $b^*$ the number of branch vertices of $T$ which lie in $B$. Clearly, $b^*\le \ell$, hence, 
$$|V(T) \cap B| = b^* + \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \leq 2\ell + e(F).$$

Therefore an upper bound for $s(F,G)$ can be obtained by counting the number of subsets of $V(G)$ containing at most $2\ell+e(F)$ vertices in $B$.
Thus
$$
s(F,G) \leq 2^{|A|} \cdot \sum_{i = 0}^{2\ell + e(F)} \binom{|B|}{i} \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell},
$$
proving the lemma.
\hfill$\blacksquare$

\medskip
\noindent
We will construct a graph $G$ for which $s(F,G) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$, via Lemma~\ref{semibip}.
Let $A,B$ be disjoint sets of vertices with $|A|=\ell-2$ and $|B| = t+1$, and let $V(G) = A \cup B$.
Add every edge to $G$ with at least one endpoint in $A$.
For any graph $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which is not complete, we claim that $G$ is $(F,t)$-locally dense.
It suffices to show that $G$ is $(K_\ell^- ,t)$-locally dense. Let $e$ be the non-adjacent pair in $K_\ell^-$ and let $xy \in E(G)$.
If $x,y \in A$, then for any of the $\binom{t+1}{2}>t$ pairs $\lbrace w,z \rbrace$ of vertices in $B$, we have that $G[A \cup \lbrace w,z \rbrace]$ is isomorphic to $K_\ell^-$ with $wz$ playing the role of $e$.
Without loss of generality, the only other case is $x \in A$, $y \in B$.
Then similarly we can choose any of the $t$ vertices $w \in B \setminus \lbrace y \rbrace$ so that $wy$ plays the role of the missing edge $e$.
Therefore every edge $xy \in E(G)$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $K_\ell^-$, and hence $F$.
Now Lemma~\ref{semibip} implies that $s_t(F) \leq s(F,G) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Construct a semi-bipartite locally dense graph and apply Lemma 4.

nodes.name: Construction
nodes.statement:
We will construct a graph $G$ for which $s(F,G) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$, via Lemma~\ref{semibip}.
Let $A,B$ be disjoint sets of vertices with $|A|=\ell-2$ and $|B| = t+1$, and let $V(G) = A \cup B$.
Add every edge to $G$ with at least one endpoint in $A$.

nodes.name: Claim: $G$ is $(F,t)$-locally dense
nodes.statement:
For any graph $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which is not complete, we claim that $G$ is $(F,t)$-locally dense.

Without loss of generality, the only other case is $x \in A$, $y \in B$.
Then similarly we can choose any of the $t$ vertices $w \in B \setminus \lbrace y \rbrace$ so that $wy$ plays the role of the missing edge $e$.
Therefore every edge $xy \in E(G)$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $K_\ell^-$, and hence $F$.

nodes.name: Reduce to $K_\ell^-$

nodes.name: Proof of part (iii)
nodes.statement:
Finally, we prove (iii).
Let ${\varepsilon} > 0$ and let $t$ be sufficiently large compared to ${\varepsilon}$.
Let $G$ be $(K_\ell^-,t)$-locally dense.
We will show that $s(K_\ell^-,G) \geq t^{(1-2{\varepsilon})(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)}$.
For each edge $e \in E(G)$, let $g(e)$ be the number of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ in $G$ which contain $e$.
Suppose first that $g(e) \geq t^{{\varepsilon}}$ for all $e \in E(G)$.
Then $G$ is $(K_{\ell-1},t^{{\varepsilon}})$-locally dense.
So, by (\ref{d}) and Theorem~\ref{btks}, $G$ contains a copy of $K_d$, where $d = (\sqrt{\ell}/3) t^{{\varepsilon}/(2(\ell-3))}$.
The same argument as (i) shows that
$$
s(K_\ell^-,G) \geq s(K_\ell,G) \geq 2^d - (d+1)^{\ell-1} \geq 2^{\frac{1}{2}t^{\frac{{\varepsilon}}{2(\ell-3)}}} > t^{\ell^2}
$$
whenever $t$ is sufficiently large compared to ${\varepsilon}$ and $\ell$ (and recall that $\ell \geq 4$).

So we may assume that there is some $e \in E(G)$ with $g(e) < t^{{\varepsilon}}$.

\begin{claim}
There is a subgraph $H$ of $G$ with vertex partition $A \cup B$ where $|A|=\ell-1$ and $|B| \geq 2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}/(\ell-1)$, such that $H[A]$ is complete and there is $z \in A$ such that $H[A\setminus \lbrace z \rbrace, B]$ is a complete bipartite graph.
\end{claim}

\medskip
\noindent
\emph{Proof.}
Let $\mathcal{J}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ containing $e$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell}^-$ containing $e$.
So $|\mathcal{J}| = g(e)$ and $|\mathcal{K}| \geq t$.
Now, every copy of $K_\ell^-$ containing $e$ contains exactly two distinct $J \in \mathcal{J}$ as subgraphs.
So, by averaging, there is some $J \in \mathcal{J}$ such that there is $\mathcal{K}' \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ with the property that $J \subseteq K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ and
\begin{equation} |\mathcal{K}'| \geq \frac{2|\mathcal{K}|}{g(e)}\ge 2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}.
\end{equation}
Every $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ has exactly one non-adjacent pair, and exactly one member of this pair lies in $V(J)$.
Averaging once again we see that there is some $z \in V(J)$ and $\mathcal{K}'' \subseteq \mathcal{K}'$ such that for all $K \in \mathcal{K}''$ every $y \in V(K)$ is incident with every $x \in V(J) \setminus \lbrace z \rbrace$; and
$$
|\mathcal{K}''| \geq \frac{|\mathcal{K}'|}{\ell-1} \stackrel{(\ref{K})}{\geq} \frac{2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}}{\ell-1}.
$$
Now, let $A := V(J)$ and let $B := \bigcup_{K \in \mathcal{K}''}V(K) \setminus V(J)$.
Every $K \in \mathcal{K''}$ contains precisely one vertex $x_K$ outside of $V(J)$ and the only non-adjacent pair in $K$ is $x_Kz$.
Therefore the vertices $x_K$ are distinct for distinct $K$.
So $|B| = |\mathcal{K}''|$, as required.
The remaining properties are clear.
\hfill$\blacksquare$

\medskip
\noindent
It will suffice to give a lower bound for $s(K_\ell^-,H)$.
We will count the number of subdivisions $T$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with specific properties.
Label the vertices of $K_\ell^-$ by $1,\ldots,\ell$, where $E(K_\ell^-) = \binom{[\ell]}{2}\setminus \lbrace \ell-1,\ell \rbrace$.
Write $A = \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_{\ell-1} := z \rbrace$.
Let $x_\ell$ and $x_{ij}$ for all $ij \in \binom{[\ell-2]}{2}$ be arbitrary distinct vertices in $B$ and let $X$ be the set consisting of these vertices.
Using these we can find a subdivision $T(X)$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with vertex set $A \cup X$, branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ and paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(K_\ell^-)$, as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item For all $i \in [\ell-1]$, the vertex $x_i \in A$ corresponds to $i \in V(K_\ell^-)$, and the vertex $x_\ell \in B$ corresponds to $\ell \in V(K_\ell^-)$.
\item For all $ij \in \binom{[\ell-2]}{2}$, each $P(i,j)$ has precisely one internal vertex $x_{ij}$, which lies in $B$. For all $i \in [\ell-2]$ and $j \in \lbrace \ell-1,\ell \rbrace$, $P(i,j)$ is the edge $x_ix_j$. 
\end{itemize}
Note that $T(X)$ exists because $H[A]$ is complete and $H[A \setminus \lbrace x_{\ell-1} \rbrace,B]$ is complete bipartite. Different choices of $X$ give rise to distinguishable $T(X)$ since $V(T(X)) = A \cup X$.
Each $X$ has order $\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1$, so
\begin{eqnarray*}
s(K_\ell^-,G) &\geq& s(K_\ell^-,H) \geq \binom{|B|}{\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1} \geq \left(\frac{2t^{1-{\varepsilon}}}{(\ell-1)\left(\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1\right)}\right)^{\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1}\\
& \geq &t^{(1-2{\varepsilon})\left(\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1\right)}= t^{(1-2{\varepsilon})(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)},
\end{eqnarray*}
completing the proof of (iii).
This concludes the proof of Theorem~\ref{main}.
\hfill$\square$
